rationale: Genesis 28:12 reads 'God’s angels were going up and down the ladder' and John 1:51 reads 'you will all see heaven open and the angels of God ascending and descending on the Son of Man' (BSB). The English differs; the Greek is closer. The Septuagint of 28:12 (Swete, on Bible Hub) has οἱ ἄγγελοι τοῦ θεοῦ ἀνέβαινον καὶ κατέβαινον ἐπ᾽ αὐτῆς, and every Greek edition of John 1:51 listed on Bible Hub has (capitalization aside) τοὺς ἀγγέλους τοῦ θεοῦ ἀναβαίνοντας καὶ καταβαίνοντας ἐπὶ τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου: the same noun phrase ('the angels of God'), the same two verbs in the same order (up before down) and the same preposition, in different grammatical forms. Where the Septuagint has a feminine pronoun (αὐτῆς), which cannot refer to Jacob and most naturally refers to the ladder (κλίμαξ), John has 'the Son of Man.' The Byzantine text, the Greek Orthodox text and the Textus Receptus add ἀπ’ ἄρτι ('from now on') after 'Truly, truly, I tell you' and before 'you will see,' which Nestle 1904, Westcott-Hort and Tischendorf lack; the shared clause is the same in all of them. No citation formula introduces the line, and John names neither Jacob nor Bethel, so the type is allusion, following conn-matt5-psalm37-meek (a formula-less near-match) and conn-gen1-word-john1. It is graded strong, not explicit, because the link rests on shared wording rather than a named reference; Ellicott, Barnes, Jamieson-Fausset-Brown, Gill, Meyer, the Expositor's Greek Testament, the Pulpit Commentary and Vincent all refer the line to Jacob's dream. It is not graded type_antitype: unlike conn-matt12-sign-jonah1, John states no 'as ... so' comparison, and whether the Son of Man answers to the ladder, to Jacob, or to neither is a dispute the lesson reports in Positions without settling it.
